title: An unauthenticated outsider eavesdrops on support conversations, becomes a chosen customer, and has the workspace mail that customer's conversation to the attacker

steps.action: open one anonymous Livechat conversation, then subscribe over DDP to another customer's room while naming the attacker's own room and token in the subscription's extraData
steps.result: a live feed of a stranger's support conversation, which is where customers type the identifiers an agent asks for

steps.action: register a fresh visitor token with the phone number harvested from that feed, so registerGuest resolves the returning customer by phone before the caller's own token
steps.result: the customer's own visitor token in the response, which is the only credential the visitor-side routes ask for

steps.action: with the stolen token, upload a file whose description is attacker HTML and request livechat/transcript for the customer's room to an attacker-controlled address
steps.result: the customer's whole conversation mailed by the workspace from its own sender address, with a live attacker link inside it

combined_impact: Proven in the lab: with no account, no credential and no victim interaction, the attacker read a stranger's support conversation as it happened, turned a phone number seen in that feed into the customer's bearer token, read their history back, posted a message into their conversation as them, and received the whole transcript by mail from the workspace's own address with a working phishing link in it. Attacker capability before: a visitor who can open its own chat. After: read and write access to any Omnichannel conversation (the stream step is per-room and repeatable), possession of a chosen customer's identity, and an exfiltration channel that carries the organisation's own SPF and DKIM alignment. Blast radius: every customer conversation on a workspace that uses Omnichannel.
preconditions: No account. Omnichannel in use (Livechat_enabled, the business feature this chain abuses; it is off by default in 9.x and on wherever the product's support offering is used), and the ability to open one Livechat conversation of the attacker's own. The run turns Omnichannel on through the workspace's own settings API and restores it.
fix_order: Fix step 2: in registerGuest (packages/omni-core/src/visitor/create.ts:105-115, VULN-001) treat an unknown token as a new visitor instead of merging into a visitor found by phone or email, and never return a token the caller did not present. One change breaks the chain, because the credential is what turns eavesdropping into impersonation and exfiltration, and it is also the only step that works from a phone number alone. Side effect: keeps the feature and removes only the weakness: returning customers who cleared their browser storage are no longer re-attached to their old visitor record automatically, which an agent does through the contact merge instead. The stream confusion (VULN-076) must be fixed as well, by authorizing against the room being subscribed to rather than the one named in extraData; on its own it stops the eavesdropping but leaves any known phone number a route to the customer's token.
